method: Per-sample local slow atomscan, cleave facts (also both extracted PEs), PE parsing, Rizin function/control-flow review, Capstone call/operand checks, configuration decoding and isolated decoder emulation. No sample entry point or Windows API was executed.

samples.identification: Lold Update Client HTTP implant and payload manager
samples.marker: Lold HTTP implant: shell tasks and WMI; add ghosting and autorun
evidence: PE64 manifest calls the program Lold Update Client; plaintext LOLD_CFG_V1 configuration contains http://217.60.102.156:8093 and a Microsoft/OneDrive installation path. The sample is unsigned.

Entry 0x2181ad947f0 reaches CRT dispatch 0x2181ad94670, then main 0x2181ad62fd0 and HTTP inbox dispatcher 0x2181ad6f780. The latter parses ping/exec/cmd/sleep/uninstall tasks retrieved from /files?prefix=inbox/. Its shell helper 0x2181ad71760 builds cmd.exe /C with the task text and calls CreateProcessW at 0x2181ad71947.

WMI subscription code constructs CommandLineEventConsumer, CommandLineTemplate, __EventFilter, __IntervalTimerInstruction and __FilterToConsumerBinding objects under root/subscription. These are implemented persistence capabilities, rather than a sandbox-only observation.

At 0x2181ad8da49 a TRUE one-byte buffer is passed to NtSetInformationFile with FileDispositionInformation=13. The same file handle is written by NtWriteFile and used for NtCreateSection with SEC_IMAGE=0x1000000 at 0x2181ad8dae4, then closed. Image mapping, entry-point computation and SetThreadContext at 0x2181ad90eed/ResumeThread support ghosted-image redirection. The existing API-bound YARA observations are retained, with a new hostile composite requiring the independently matched HTTP shell implant.

Run-key registration helper near 0x2181ad747b0 quotes the configured image path and writes REG_SZ through the opened HKCU key at 0x2181ad7496e. Own-image path lookup and CopyFileW coexist with the fixed platform Run path; the new hostile rule reuses this existing neutral profile and the HTTP implant predicate.

Task Scheduler COM setup at 0x2181ad74a7e binds CLSID_TaskScheduler and IID_ITaskService to CoCreateInstance. The same routine requests trigger type 9 (logon) at 0x2181ad7502b and registers the task using flags 6 (create/update), interactive token type 3, and the ITaskFolder RegisterTaskDefinition vtable slot at 0x2181ad75760. The new notable rule binds both GUID operands and the imported CoCreateInstance callee, and requires the nearby trigger/registration code. It claims code presence, not runtime success.

The executable exposes clear native instructions and a plaintext configuration. The high-entropy .ndata region was inspected, but its purpose was not established; no encryption or executable-payload claim was added from entropy alone. Optional launch backends and persistence modes do not establish which branch succeeded on a victim.
samples.balance_and_missing_context: An updater can use HTTP, COM and autorun. Here a reusable shell-task channel, multiple concealed persistence backends, ghosted-image launch code and deceptive OneDrive packaging tip the judgment to MALICIOUS. The matching C2 has external corroboration, but the verdict rests on code. Deployment authorization, selected optional backends and runtime success remain unknown.

samples.identification: Modified XMRig executable with appended Go downloader and Cobalt Strike Beacon
samples.marker: Modified XMRig/Beacon: self-clone execution; correct API profile
evidence: PE64 has readable, already-unpacked native code in UPX0 and a modified main at 0x14002add4, reachable through the CRT entry dispatch. Section names alone were not treated as packing.

Main opens argv[0], reads its complete bytes and interprets the final eight bytes as two counters. It decrements a counter, writes executable copies under C:/Windows/System/, appends rewritten counters, calls CreateProcessW at 0x14002b01d and loops at 0x14002b023. This added replication code precedes normal XMRig controller/miner work.

The embedded XMRig configuration enables cn/r mining at 3.120.209.58:8080 with user/pass x and donation zero. Mining alone is dual use; the custom system-directory clone-launch loop plus the embedded implant tips the artifact to malicious.

Appended PE at 0xfc400 is a Go executable. COFF symbols identify main.checkForAdmin, main.main, main.GetArchive and main.Extract. main.checkForAdmin probes PHYSICALDRIVE0; the non-admin branch requests normal runAs elevation through PowerShell, not a UAC bypass. GetArchive binds HTTP response data to a local file; main extracts an S3 ZIP under C:/G DATA Security Software/, deletes its temporary archive and starts AVK.exe. The remotely named archive was not fetched or executed, so its final payload identity is unresolved.

Appended PE at 0x5b8601 is an x86 DLL exporting _ReflectiveLoader@4. XOR-0x69 decoding of its typed settings at relative offset 0x2f228 yields DNS mode, port 443, sleep 5000 ms, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top, Amazon-shaped HTTP templates and rundll32 spawn paths. Native DNS APIs, token launch code, reflective loading and PEB/ROR13 resolution corroborate Beacon identity.

Beacon includes WriteProcessMemory at 0x10005785, SuspendThread at 0x1000611e, SetThreadContext/ResumeThread at 0x1000634e/0x1000635e, and token-open/duplicate/impersonation launch paths near 0x10009d4a. The moved suspicious import profile does not itself bind those APIs into a chain or require replacing a process image. Its matcher, effective scope, confidence and severity were preserved.

The appended executables are statically present; the outer file does not prove they are invoked. Its text-like final trailer yields large counter values, so the clone-launch path may fail. No rule or verdict depends on observing success.
samples.balance_and_missing_context: XMRig and Cobalt Strike have authorized uses, and the Go downloader requests ordinary user-approved elevation. The custom executable replication into a system directory, configured mining and appended implant together tip this packaged artifact to MALICIOUS. No deployment authorization, successful replication or remote-archive payload identity is established.

samples.identification: Native HTTP RAT masquerading as Microsoft Word
samples.marker: Word-disguised HTTP RAT: command execution; add Run-key coverage
evidence: Unsigned PE32 version data claims Microsoft Word/WINWORD.exe/Microsoft Office 2016, while the executable implements a hidden HTTP command agent. This contradicts its claimed application purpose.

Entry 0x405b22 calls main 0x404551. Configuration loader 0x4032c0 concatenates four stored segments, XORs with 0x42 and decompresses them using the routine at 0x404b97. Only that self-contained decoding routine was emulated, without Windows APIs or execution of the program. The recovered 1580-byte configuration contains i.assmio.com, m.assmio.com and UTF-16 WINWORD.

HTTP worker 0x4037cb receives a response, validates its three-word checksum and switches on command IDs 1000..1019 at 0x4039c5. Tasks reach file enumeration/read/write, process operations, shutdown/restart and shell helpers. Routine 0x404e6a builds the System32/cmd.exe path on the stack, creates inheritable pipes and launches the shell at 0x404f6e; task handling reads and returns its output.

Run-key helper 0x402ad6 builds SOFTWARE/Microsoft/Windows/CurrentVersion/Run as UTF-16 stack stores, opens HKCU at 0x402c4d and writes a REG_SZ image command at 0x402c90. Its self-copy/install callers use the current module path. The new stack-construction atom is neutral; the hostile persistence composite also requires the independent HTTP RAT dispatcher and registry open/write APIs.

Self-cleanup helper 0x40317d obtains its own module path, constructs cmd/ping/del text as stack immediates and invokes WinExec at 0x40324e. Existing self-deletion and Office-masquerade detections remain accurate and retained. Existing XOR-transform and dynamic-WinInet capability detections were also preserved.
samples.balance_and_missing_context: A remote administration program can expose execution and file operations legitimately. This unsigned program misrepresents itself as Word, conceals its controller configuration and installation strings, installs a self-copy for logon and erases its original image while operating an HTTP shell/file task channel. Those combined behaviors tip the judgment to MALICIOUS; deployment authorization and runtime success are unknown.
